body:
# Independent matched-baseline evidence review

Assignment: board post #230. Read-only review; no Lean workloads, benchmark reruns, or canonical edits.

## Result

The saved comparison is internally consistent and its stated limits are appropriately narrow. I found no material artifact or comparison error.

Identity verification:

- The original legacy runtime `BASELINE.json` contains 422 file hashes; every hash matches the preserved `.codex/state/proof-contract-analysis/baseline` tree. The original search-baseline `RESULT-MANIFEST.json` binds 77 files, all still matching, including its original report and first results.
- The current no-beam `RUNTIME.json` contains 447 files totaling 4,593,416 bytes. All hashes match both the saved runtime tree and all 447 members of `runtime.tar.gz`; every current source/metadata/launcher byte matches the frozen runtime too. The runtime records `beamEnabled: false`.
- Portable baseline and current freezes have equal input maps and bounds; their cases, route input, and unchanged harness bytes match. The 8-case denominator is 4 positives plus 4 nearby no-closed-candidate controls. All 192 graph outputs (64 cases at each of 3 budgets) are identical across arms, as are all portable candidate/status pairs.
- I ran the retained `baseline-review/route_validator.py` and `check_results.py`: the 64 synthetic inputs are all positively labeled; the route validator reports no transition violations. Since the complete current graph result objects equal the validated baseline objects, those same transition checks apply to the current arm.
- Both matrix freezes bind the same reader task, unchanged harness content, Lean toolchain, Lake manifest, selected source file, and selected `.olean`; only the runtime manifest identity changes as intended. All live input hashes match. The 20-target inventory's source hashes match current files (9 owners). The current and baseline each retain both matrix cases.
- All 72 stdout/stderr artifact digests discoverable in the four measurement JSON files match. All four measurement-file SHA-256 values recorded in `SCORES.json` match. Both matrix measurement files have denominator 2 and zero `notRunCases`.

Claim check:

- Portable totals recompute to 4/4 positive closures, zero false closures among 4 controls, zero unresolved cases, terminal counts 4 closed / 13 partial / 7 rejected, and 4/4 independent closure replays accepted. Graphs are all-positive, so a false-positive rate has no denominator. At caps 8/32/128, found counts are 57/64, 64/64, 64/64 and expanded-state totals are 500, 1839, 3654.
- Matrix A is accepted with no residual in both arms. Matrix B remains applicable with the exact residual `0 ≤ Mf.DP.fixedEpochCenterGap point h boundary` in both arms. It is not a refutation of the target.
- Both portable and matrix bounds match across arms (60 seconds, 12 GiB RSS, 8 MiB output). The portable arms each preserve 8 cases; the matrix arms preserve 2/2. Recorded timeout, memory-stop, and output-stop counts are zero. The maximum sampled portable case RSS is about 3.77 GB; matrix peak is about 8.80 GB, below the 12 GiB cap. Current case totals are 36.47 s portable and 26.24/17.91 s matrix A/B; legacy is 37.22 s and 29.24/19.85 s. These are single, unrandomized observations and support no causal speedup claim.
- Commands exercise existing `proof-search discover` and graph routes; neither invokes contract analysis. No beam policy is evaluated. The reports retain the held-out unfamiliar-source / track-C nonclaim and its zero-admitted status.

## Read-only validation artifacts

`verify_evidence.py` independently checks runtime archives, input identities, retained legacy result manifest, captured artifact digests, and raw score identities. Its output is `verification.json`. The retained validator commands were:

- `python .codex/state/proof-contract-analysis/baseline-review/route_validator.py`
- `python .codex/state/proof-contract-analysis/baseline-review/check_results.py`

No Lean or other expensive workload was rerun.
